detail.longDescription: I have a PHP application with this folder structure: modules/ mymodule/ samefile.html (not tracked by git where I develop new features) src/ samefile.html (tracked by git) This module is part of another git repository : MainApp (Entire App GIT Repo) ->Module (One Module of the MainApp GIT Repo) I am looking for a cleaner way to copy to src/ folder the files I have changed, taking care to not push unwanted changes to git. Outside src/ folder I have the same files of the src/ folder What I change I can see reflected in my http://localhost on my machine. Only files inside src/ folder are tracked by git , which is where I do a git pull . The structure is: modules/mymodule/src and modules/mymodule/<files-mirroring-src-folder> I do git pull inside src/ folder. Outside of the src/ folder: I do a backup copy of the modules/mymodule/samefile.html Copy the files from src/ to mymodule/ to maintain integrity, Make the changes to the files And copy to src/ folder again Is there a better way using git or another tool? I am using using meldmerge and comparing directories outside of the application to not change the encoding too. Inside of the src/ folder: add , commit and push .
